sources.title: İŞKUR (Türkiye İş Kurumu / Turkish Employment Agency) — Geleceğin Meslekleri (Occupations of the Future)
sources.claim_supported: Official Turkish government list of 93 named future/emerging occupations, fetched and read directly (PDF). Confirms official recognition of software engineering, computer engineering, AI, data analysis, cybersecurity, civil/electrical/mechanical/mechatronics/telecom/mining/geomatics engineering, chemistry, environmental engineering, solar-panel installation, e-commerce, marketing, HR, and digital marketing/social media roles as future-oriented in Turkey.
sources.limitations: A named list only, no per-occupation skills/salary/education detail. Absence of an occupation from this specific 93-item list is not evidence that occupation is unrecognized in Turkey. Found and read successfully after two other Turkish government sources (YÖK Atlas Meslek Atlası, MYK vocational-standard PDFs) failed to yield readable content via WebFetch/search this session (JS-rendering and PDF-encoding issues respectively) — Turkish official sources are confirmed harder to access programmatically than US/UK/EU equivalents, a real infrastructure finding in its own right.

sources.title: Cross-referenced UK Year Group / US Grade / age conversion resources
sources.claim_supported: Approximate correspondence between years-until-graduation, US grade labels, UK Year labels, and IB staging.
sources.limitations: No single official source publishes a cross-country correspondence table (each government publishes only its own system); convergent across multiple independent sources but not a primary official source.

sources.title: College Board SAT Suite test dates and grade-by-grade guidance
sources.claim_supported: PSAT 10 in sophomore spring, PSAT/NMSQT in junior fall; first official SAT typically junior spring; retakes into senior fall.
sources.limitations: The 'most sophomores aren't ready for the SAT' narrative framing is secondary-sourced, not an official College Board statement verbatim.

sources.title: IB Diploma Programme subject-selection timeline (cross-referenced school/counseling guidance)
sources.claim_supported: IB subject selection occurs at the Grade 10/11 transition; DP Year 1/2 structure (subject selection + CAS/IA start in Y1, final submissions/exams in Y2).
sources.limitations: No single official IBO page found with the complete timeline; convergent across secondary sources only.

sources.title: Pre-college research program eligibility patterns (Harvard Pre-College, Stanford SIMR, Davidson Research Initiative, Rockefeller, Max Planck Florida)
sources.claim_supported: Selective pre-college research programs commonly gate on 'rising junior/senior' status (roughly 2-1 years from graduation), age 16-19.
sources.limitations: Pattern-level confidence only; individual program specifics should be re-verified against each program's own official page before citing to a student — that verification is the separate opportunity-acquisition workstream's job, not this research package's.

sources.title: Turkey's Student Selection and Placement System (YKS) — ÖSYM-administered
sources.claim_supported: YKS is a centralized, standardized-exam-based placement system (TYT/AYT/YDT sessions), with placement by score-ranked preference matching rather than a holistic application file.
sources.limitations: ÖSYM's own site (osym.gov.tr) not directly fetched this pass; exact current-year exam format should be re-verified there before citing as current to a student.

sources.title: UCAS super-curricular vs. extracurricular distinction; 2026-entry personal statement format
sources.claim_supported: UCAS draws an explicit distinction between subject-relevant 'super-curricular' engagement and general 'extracurricular' activity; the 2026-entry personal statement format is built around three subject-focused questions.
sources.limitations: The peer branch's `01-development-taxonomy.md` may not independently cover UCAS at all (it appears US-source-focused) — flagged as a possible coverage gap, not assumed resolved.

sources.title: O*NET — Computer and Information Research Scientists (15-1221.00); Software Developers (15-1252.00)
sources.claim_supported: Core skills/knowledge for computing occupations: quantitative reasoning, inductive/deductive reasoning, written/oral communication.
sources.limitations: US Dept. of Labor-sponsored database — US-specific occupational framing.

sources.title: BLS Occupational Outlook Handbook — Computer and Information Technology Occupations

sources.limitations: US-specific; not assumed to generalize internationally.

sources.title: National Careers Service — digital/computing job profiles (app developer, web developer, computer games developer)
sources.claim_supported: UK's official careers-service equivalent to BLS/O*NET for computing roles; qualifications, salary, progression per profile.
sources.limitations: UK-specific (run by England's Department for Education).

sources.title: ESCO — European Skills, Competences, Qualifications and Occupations
sources.claim_supported: EU-wide occupation/skills classification (~3,000 occupations, ~14,000 skills, 28+ languages), built for cross-border job/training matching.
sources.limitations: A classification/vocabulary, not a narrative careers-guidance source with growth/salary data the way BLS/NCS are.
used_in: referenced from all 9 of this session's family docs' §7 country-notes sections

sources.title: BLS OOH — Mathematicians and Statisticians
sources.claim_supported: Core skills: programming, staying current with statistical methods; communication skill differentiates job prospects.

sources.title: BLS OOH — Actuaries
sources.claim_supported: 22% projected growth 2024-2034; core skills in math/statistics/business and analytical pattern-recognition.
sources.limitations: US-specific; growth statistic is an aggregate labor-market figure, not an individual-student probability.

sources.title: Society of Actuaries / Casualty Actuarial Society — actuarial credentialing path
sources.claim_supported: Actuarial credentialing (ASA/FSA) is exam-sequence-based (VEE course-credit + preliminary/fellowship exams), not gated behind one specific university major.
sources.limitations: US/Canada-specific; UK (IFoA) is a genuinely separate body, not interchangeable.

sources.title: Institute and Faculty of Actuaries (UK) — route to becoming an actuary
sources.claim_supported: UK's actuarial chartered body; exam/course structure (core technical/applications, specialist stages) plus 3+ years qualifying experience and PPD.
sources.limitations: UK-specific; formed 2010 from a merger of two historically separate bodies.

sources.title: BLS OOH — Physicists and Astronomers
sources.claim_supported: Physics/astronomy degrees' skills transfer broadly beyond the named occupation; BLS states this explicitly.
sources.limitations: The fetched snapshot cited a 2018-2028 projection cycle — BLS updates on a rolling cycle, so the specific growth percentage should be re-verified against the live page before quoting as current.

sources.title: BLS OOH — Chemists and Materials Scientists
sources.claim_supported: Teamwork/leadership skill named explicitly (chemists typically work on research teams) — corrective to a 'solitary bench scientist' assumption.
sources.limitations: US-specific.

sources.title: American Chemical Society — US National Chemistry Olympiad, ChemClubs, Project SEED
sources.claim_supported: USNCO's local->national->international-team structure; Project SEED is an ACS-sponsored paid summer research program for economically disadvantaged students.

sources.claim_supported: UK chemist profile names Chartered Chemist (CChem)/Chartered Scientist (CSci) as a career-progression track, not an entry gate.

sources.title: UK Biologist job profile (via Careerpilot, presenting NCS-aligned content)

sources.title: BLS Career Outlook — Engineers: Employment, pay, and outlook; BLS OOH Aerospace Eng. Technologists/Technicians
sources.claim_supported: Applied math/physics as a foundation across ME/CE/AE/EE; design + troubleshooting skill for aerospace specifically.

sources.title: BLS OOH — Mechanical Engineers; Aerospace Engineers; Architecture and Engineering Occupations overview
sources.claim_supported: 2024-2034 growth: ME +9%, CE +5%, AE +6%; civil is the largest engineering occupation by new-job count; aerospace growth drivers named (efficiency redesigns, satellite-launch cost, small-sat viability).

sources.title: NSPE — How to Get Licensed / What Is a PE?; NCEES Exams
sources.claim_supported: US PE licensure: accredited degree -> FE exam -> 4 years supervised experience -> PE exam, standardized nationally via NCEES.
sources.limitations: US-specific; explicitly not assumed to describe UK/Turkey/EU systems (see S-CENG, S-TMMOB for those).

sources.title: Engineering Council / IET — Chartered Engineer (CEng)
sources.claim_supported: UK's CEng credential: accredited MEng (or bachelor's+master's) + demonstrated professional competence over years, assessed via professional review — not exam-sequence-based like the US PE system.
sources.limitations: UK-specific; administered through subfield-specific licensed institutions (IET, ICE, IMechE, RAeS, etc.), not one single body.

sources.title: TMMOB (Türk Mühendis ve Mimar Odaları Birliği) official site; Law No. 6235
sources.claim_supported: Turkey has a legally-mandated engineer/architect title-protection system (Law No. 3458) administered through 24 discipline-specific TMMOB chambers (700,000+ members) — chamber registration required to practice/use the title.
sources.limitations: Turkey-specific; a genuinely distinct structure from both US PE and UK CEng, not a variant of either.

sources.title: BLS OOH — Bioengineers and Biomedical Engineers
sources.claim_supported: Growth driven by new medical-device technology and an aging population; graduate degree typical for leading a research team, not for entry-level industry roles.
sources.limitations: US-specific.

sources.title: Regulatory-affairs/FDA-compliance career framing (secondary corroboration)
